title: Updates.reloadAsync() crashes if called during first startup
body: I use `Updates.reloadAsync()` on logout so the app restarts with cleared reducers. In an iOS production build using Expo SDK 47, calling it during the app's first launch crashes the app; after reopening the same app, the same call works. Android does not appear to crash. This also happens when `reloadAsync()` is called directly without applying an update. If an update is available and I call `checkForUpdateAsync()`, `fetchUpdateAsync()`, and then `reloadAsync()`, that reload succeeds, but another direct `reloadAsync()` during that first launch can still crash. Restarting the app once prevents the crash. The app uses the managed workflow with Expo 47.0.13, React Native 0.70.5, and production builds made with EAS.

symptoms_visible: On the first launch of my iOS production build, calling `Updates.reloadAsync()` directly during logout closes the app.
After I reopen the app, the same `reloadAsync()` call works normally.
A check, fetch, and reload sequence for an available update succeeds, but another direct reload during that first launch can still close the app.
One of our affected apps is published on the App Store, so you can install that released build yourself and watch it close the first time you log out after logging in.
N0.label: N0 first-launch iOS reload crash reported

symptoms_visible: A blank SDK 47 app with `expo-updates` closes when I press a control that calls `reloadAsync()` on its first launch; after reopening it, the same control reloads normally.
N1.label: N1 minimal SDK 47 reproduction described

symptoms_visible: The iOS process aborts during the first-start reload; one crash report says `JSCRuntime destroyed with a dangling API object`.
In the update-on-startup version of the problem, the app can crash at `reloadAsync()` or hang while checking or fetching the update.
N2.label: N2 runtime abort and startup update setup collected

symptoms_visible: After upgrading the app to SDK 48 and making a new build, calling `reloadAsync()` on the first launch no longer closes the app.
N3.label: N3 SDK 48 build avoids reporter's crash

symptoms_visible: My working SDK 48 build uses the default Hermes engine and reloads normally on first launch.
In an affected SDK 48 build explicitly configured for JSC, the direct reload still closed the app; changing that build to Hermes stopped the crash.
N4.label: N4 engine difference established

symptoms_visible: On a fresh installation of the rebuilt iOS app, the first-launch logout reload and the check, fetch, and reload sequence both complete without closing the app.
N_terminal.label: terminal first-launch reload works

question_patterns: Can you reproduce this in a minimal SDK 47 project with only Expo, React Native, and expo-updates?
What exact steps reproduce the crash in a blank production build?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. I can create a blank SDK 47 Expo app, install and configure `expo-updates`, add an `onPress` that calls `Updates.reloadAsync()`, make an iOS production build, and install it. On the first launch, pressing it closes the app. After reopening the app, pressing the same element works.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I cannot reproduce it in a blank app; it only happens after my production app initializes its state-management and animation libraries.
The same blank SDK 47 app reproduces it when built locally in Release configuration rather than through EAS.

edges.comment: Reporter supplied the minimal steps in c4. No pushed OTA update is required for the direct-reload reproduction.

question_patterns: Can you share the iOS crash type and the relevant assertion or stack line?
What does the crash report show when `reloadAsync()` closes the app?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The iOS crash is `EXC_CRASH (SIGABRT)`. In one of our logs the assertion is `JSCRuntime destroyed with a dangling API object`, from `~JSCRuntime` in `JSCRuntime.cpp`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The process is terminated by iOS for memory pressure and there is no JavaScript-runtime assertion.
It is still SIGABRT with the same dangling JSC API-object assertion, but the triggered thread number differs.

question_patterns: Is expo-updates configured to check automatically on launch while your JavaScript also calls the update APIs during startup?
Please show the startup update code and the `updates` section of your Expo config.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I never set `checkAutomatically`; the `updates` section of my Expo config only has the update URL and `fallbackToCacheTimeout: 0`. In the affected startup flow I hold the splash screen with `preventAutoHideAsync()` and then call `checkForUpdateAsync()`, and if an update is available, `fetchUpdateAsync()` and `reloadAsync()` from an initialization effect, before the splash screen is released.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Automatic checks are disabled with `ON_ERROR_RECOVERY`, and no JavaScript update API is called until several minutes after startup.
The splash screen uses a different background color in the staging build.

edges.comment: Crash evidence and startup-update code came from additional affected users and are folded into the simulated user side. The answers retain the raw assertion and configuration; the concurrency diagnosis remains engineer-side.

solution.intent: Move the affected SDK 47 iOS app to an SDK 48 build using its default Hermes runtime, then retest a direct `reloadAsync()` on the first launch.
solution.concrete_example: Upgrade the project to Expo SDK 48, regenerate the native production build with the default Hermes engine, install it fresh, and invoke the same direct `Updates.reloadAsync()` action on the first launch.

edges.comment: Reporter confirmed in c9 that a newly built SDK 48 app did not crash when `reloadAsync()` was invoked on its first launch.

question_patterns: Does the working SDK 48 build use Hermes or JSC?
When you upgraded to SDK 48, did you retain JSC or start using the default Hermes engine?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I did not keep JSC configured. SDK 48 uses Hermes by default, so the working build is now on Hermes.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The working SDK 48 build explicitly sets `jsEngine: 'jsc'`; switching between JSC and Hermes has no effect.
Hermes is explicitly set in my config rather than selected through the SDK 48 default.

edges.comment: Engineer asked the reporter this directly in c13; the reporter confirmed Hermes in c14. A later affected user reported that SDK 48 with explicit JSC still crashed and that switching that build to Hermes fixed it, so the engine distinction is retained as volunteered evidence.

solution.intent: Use a current Expo native build with Hermes and ensure only one update-check path runs during startup, preventing `reloadAsync()` from tearing down the JavaScript runtime while native automatic update work is still in progress.
solution.concrete_example: Keep the SDK 48+ build on Hermes. If JavaScript performs the startup `checkForUpdateAsync()`/`fetchUpdateAsync()` flow, set `updates.checkAutomatically` to `ON_ERROR_RECOVERY` and rebuild so the native automatic check does not run concurrently. Alternatively, retain the automatic check and react to `Updates.useUpdateEvents`, fetching and reloading only after an `UPDATE_AVAILABLE` event. Then verify the production build from a fresh installation by exercising the first-launch logout and OTA-update paths.
solution.inference_hint: The user supplied first-launch timing, startup code/configuration, the raw JSC assertion, and comparative Hermes results. The conclusion that the native automatic startup check runs simultaneously with the early JavaScript update calls was drawn by the Expo engineer in c22 and c28; tying that overlap to the JSC dangling-API assertion the user pasted is a further engineer-side inference that the thread never states outright. Neither may be placed in a clarification answer.

edges.comment: Technical resolution from c22 and c28: avoid simultaneous native automatic and JavaScript-driven startup update operations. Hermes also resolves the reporter's direct SDK 47/JSC failure pattern, while SDK 48 alone is insufficient if JSC is explicitly retained.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the first-start failure mechanism: the expo-updates native automatic startup check runs at the same time as the early JavaScript update calls, and a `reloadAsync()` issued inside that window aborts the process — on JSC the abort surfaces as the dangling API-object assertion the user reported.
Diagnosis must be grounded in the first-launch-only behavior, the raw JSC SIGABRT assertion, the automatic-check plus JavaScript startup flow, and the SDK 48/Hermes comparison.

The fix must be delivered in a new native build and must settle on a single startup update orchestration strategy: either disable normal automatic checks with `checkAutomatically: "ON_ERROR_RECOVERY"` when JavaScript manages checks, or retain automatic checking and respond through update events.
Must not claim that merely changing the SDK version while explicitly retaining JSC is sufficient; an affected SDK 48 JSC build still crashed, while switching it to Hermes stopped the crash.
Must not treat an available OTA update as necessary to reproduce the original direct `reloadAsync()` crash; the blank SDK 47 reproduction crashes without a pushed update.
Must ask the user to verify both the first-launch direct reload and the normal check/fetch/reload path on a fresh installation of the rebuilt app before declaring resolution.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced Expo application developer comfortable with EAS production builds, expo-updates APIs, runtime configuration, and creating a minimal SDK project, but initially unsure about the native first-start behavior.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct and technically detailed; supplies exact reproduction sequences, distinguishes direct reloads from OTA update reloads, and reports comparative platform and SDK results.
